text: Wildlife around the world faces many problems today. Many species of animals are losing their natural habitat because people are cutting down forests and building cities. Some animals, like certain mammals and birds, are now endangered, which means there are very few of them left in the wild. If we do not protect them, they could become extinct, like the dinosaurs many years ago. Zoos try to help. In many zoos, workers breed endangered animals so that more babies are born and the species can survive. For example, a bird might build a nest in the zoo, just like it would in the wild. However, many people believe that a cage is not a real home, and wild animals are happier in nature. In the wild, predators hunt other animals, called prey, to find food. Some animals, like certain birds, migrate to warmer places every winter to survive the cold weather. Every animal, from a small insect to a large mammal with thick fur, has an important place in nature. We must work together to protect wildlife and their habitats for the future.
